fullPassage:
Hello, first-year students. I'm your school counselor, Hannah Kim. How is your new school life? You may have experienced a situation where things didn't go as you expected at school. Have you ever wondered why this happens? Let's take a look at the following two cases.

The first case is about a student named Hajun. On the first day of school, Hajun's homeroom teacher introduced several school clubs. At that time, Hajun didn't have a particular preference for any of them. He thought that any indoor club would be okay since he was not an outdoor person. Can you guess what happened on the day of choice? He joined the soccer club. What made him choose soccer?

Well, a few days before submitting his application, he heard that the soccer club was so popular that half of his classmates were applying for it. This made him think that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club just because others did so. However, after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer was not for him. In the end, he regretted his decision.

Why do you think this happened? Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be excluded from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect." Following the crowd, of course, does not always lead to negative consequences, but it can lead to regret. So, how can you make your own choices? The first thing is to know what you really want. Although it might be different from your friends', don't be afraid to make your own choice. As long as you make the right choice for you, you will be happy about your decision.

Now, let's look at another case, one about Yubin. One day, Yubin told me about her first science quiz. Science was the subject that she struggled with the most. Since she wanted to get a good grade, she made a thorough study plan for herself. Yet, every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead. For instance, she cleaned her desk or texted her friends. These activities distracted her from studying, and in the end, she got a bad grade. She was frustrated that she continuously engaged in behaviors unhelpful for accomplishing her task.

When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in the short term. However, be careful! It could lead to repeated failures in certain tasks that you are not confident in doing.

If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually stop your self-handicapping.

As first-year students in high school, you'll sometimes face difficult moments. It is not unusual because everyone goes through difficult times. Even though you feel disappointed with your choices or behaviors, don't let yourself feel down. The most important thing is figuring out your own way to overcome your negative feelings. It will make your school life much more enjoyable. If you feel worried, remember that you are not alone. You have friends, teachers, and me. Good luck in this exciting new chapter of your life.

questions.passage: The first case is about a student named Hajun. On the first day of school, Hajun's homeroom teacher introduced several school clubs. At that time, Hajun didn't have a (A)[particular / general] preference for any of them. He thought that any indoor club would be okay since he was not an (B)[outdoor / athletic] person. Can you guess what happened on the day of (C)[choice / exam]? He joined the soccer club.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 첫 번째 사례는 하준이라는 학생에 관한 것이다. 하준의 담임 선생님이 여러 동아리를 소개했다. 그 당시 하준은 어느 것에도 특별한 선호가 없었다. 그는 야외 활동을 좋아하는 사람이 아니어서 실내 동아리면 괜찮다고 생각했다. 선택의 날에 무슨 일이 일어났을까?
det.analysis:
✅ (A) particular(특별한): didn't have a particular preference — 특정 선호가 없었다는 문맥. general(일반적인)은 부적합.
✅ (B) outdoor(야외의): indoor club이 괜찮다고 했으므로 outdoor person이 아니라는 문맥. athletic(운동하는)은 가능해 보이지만 원문은 outdoor.
✅ (C) choice(선택): 동아리를 '선택'하는 날. exam(시험)은 문맥 부적합.
det.tip: particular preference: 특별한 선호 / outdoor person: 야외 활동을 좋아하는 사람 / day of choice: 선택의 날

questions.passage: Well, a few days before submitting his application, he heard that the soccer club was so (A)[popular / unpopular] that half of his classmates were applying for it. This made him think that the soccer club was something (B)[special / ordinary]. With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club just because others did so. However, after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer was not for him. In the end, he (C)[regretted / celebrated] his decision.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 지원서 제출 며칠 전, 그는 축구 동아리가 너무 인기가 있어서 반 친구의 절반이 지원한다는 것을 들었다. 이로 인해 축구 동아리가 특별한 것이라고 생각하게 되었다. 그러나 동아리에 가입한 후, 축구가 자신에게 맞지 않는다는 것을 깨달았다. 결국 그는 자신의 결정을 후회했다.
det.analysis:
✅ (A) popular: so popular that ~ (너무 인기 있어서). unpopular이면 반 친구가 지원하는 문맥과 모순.
✅ (B) special: 인기가 있어서 '특별한' 것이라 생각. ordinary(평범한)는 반대.
✅ (C) regretted: 축구가 자신에게 맞지 않아서 '후회'. celebrated(축하했다)는 반대.
det.tip: so ~ that ...: 너무 ~해서 ... / sign up for: ~에 등록하다 / regret one's decision: 결정을 후회하다

questions.passage: Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be (A)[excluded / included] from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the (B)[crowd / leader], rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect." Following the crowd, of course, does not always lead to (C)[negative / positive] consequences, but it can lead to regret.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 심리학자들은 사람들이 다른 사람들이 하고 있다는 이유만으로 특정 행동에 참여하는 경향이 있다고 말한다. 또한 사람들은 또래에게서 배제되는 것을 원하지 않는다. 이러한 심리적 요인들은 사람들로 하여금 스스로 행동하기보다 군중을 따르게 만든다. 군중을 따르는 것이 항상 부정적인 결과를 초래하는 것은 아니지만, 후회로 이어질 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ (A) excluded: 또래에게서 '배제되길' 원하지 않는다. included(포함되다)는 반대.
✅ (B) crowd: follow the crowd(군중을 따르다) = 편승효과의 핵심. leader(지도자)는 문맥 부적합.
✅ (C) negative: 부정적 결과를 '항상' 초래하는 것은 아니지만 후회 가능. positive는 but 이하와 모순.
❌ ② included – crowd – positive: (A)가 반대, (C)가 반대
❌ ③ excluded – leader – positive: (B)와 (C)가 반대
❌ ④ included – leader – negative: (A)와 (B)가 반대
det.tip: be excluded from: ~에서 배제되다 / follow the crowd: 군중을 따르다 / bandwagon effect: 편승 효과

questions.passage: Well, a few days before submitting his application, he heard that the soccer club was so popular that half of his classmates were ①<u>applying</u> for it. This made him think that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he ②<u>signed</u> up for the soccer club just because others did so. However, after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer was not for him. In the end, he ③<u>regretted</u> his decision. Why do you think this happened? Psychologists say that people tend to ④<u>avoid</u> certain behaviors just because others are doing them.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 반 친구 절반이 ①<u>지원하고</u> 있었다. 그는 축구 동아리에 ②<u>등록했다</u>. 결국 결정을 ③<u>후회했다</u>. 심리학자들은 사람들이 다른 사람들이 한다는 이유만으로 특정 행동에 ④<u>피한다</u>고 말한다.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ avoid(피하다): 원문은 engage in(참여하다). 다른 사람들이 하니까 '참여'하는 것이지 '피하는' 것이 아님.
❌ ① applying: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ② signed: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ③ regretted: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: engage in: ~에 참여하다 ↔ avoid: ~을 피하다 / sign up for: ~에 등록하다 / apply for: ~에 지원하다

questions.passage: When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create ①<u>obstacles</u> to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make ②<u>excuses</u> for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from ③<u>lowering</u> their self-esteem. This might work in the ④<u>long</u> term. However, be careful!
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 사람들이 과제를 잘 수행할 자신감이 없을 때, 성공에 대한 ①<u>장애물</u>을 만들 가능성이 있다. 자기 핸디캡핑은 저조한 수행에 대해 ②<u>변명</u>을 할 수 있게 해준다. 이 변명들은 저조한 결과가 자존감을 ③<u>낮추는</u> 것을 막는다. 이것은 ④<u>장기적으로</u> 효과가 있을지도 모른다.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ long(긴, 장기적): 원문은 short(짧은, 단기적). 자기 핸디캡핑은 '단기적으로' 효과가 있을 수 있다는 문맥. 바로 뒤에 'However, be careful!'로 경고.
❌ ① obstacles: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ② excuses: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ③ lowering: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: in the short term: 단기적으로 ↔ in the long term: 장기적으로 / self-handicapping: 자기 핸디캡핑

questions.passage: If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the ①<u>process</u> than the outcome may ②<u>ease</u> the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more ③<u>discouraged</u> to try to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually ④<u>stop</u> your self-handicapping.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 자기 핸디캡핑을 하고 있다면, 결과를 과정보다 중요하게 여기기 때문일 수 있다. 결과보다 ①<u>과정</u>에 더 집중하면 잘 해야 한다는 압박감을 ②<u>줄일</u> 수 있다. 따라서 도전적인 과제를 시도하려는 마음이 더 ③<u>꺾일</u> 수 있다. 이것이 결국 자기 핸디캡핑을 ④<u>멈출</u> 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ③ discouraged(낙담한): 원문은 encouraged(고무된). 압박감이 줄어들면 더 '격려받는' 느낌이 들어 도전적 과제를 시도할 수 있다는 문맥.
❌ ① process: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ② ease: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ stop: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: encouraged(격려받은) ↔ discouraged(낙담한) / ease the pressure: 압박을 줄이다 / accordingly: 따라서

questions.passage: Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be excluded from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "__________ effect."
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사람들이 다른 사람들이 한다는 이유만으로 특정 행동에 참여하는 경향이 있다. 이러한 심리적 요인들은 사람들로 하여금 군중을 따르게 만든다. 이 현상을 편승 효과라고 부른다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① bandwagon: bandwagon effect(편승 효과) — 다수가 하니까 따라하는 현상. 원문 그대로.
❌ ② butterfly: butterfly effect(나비 효과) — 작은 변화가 큰 결과를 낳는 현상. 문맥 부적합.
❌ ③ domino: domino effect(도미노 효과) — 연쇄 반응. 문맥 부적합.
❌ ④ snowball: snowball effect(눈덩이 효과) — 점점 커지는 현상. 문맥 부적합.
det.tip: bandwagon effect: 편승 효과 (밴드왜건 = 악단 마차. 행렬에 뛰어오르듯 다수를 따르는 현상)

questions.passage: When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their __________.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자신감이 없을 때 성공에 대한 장애물을 만든다. 자기 핸디캡핑은 저조한 수행에 대한 변명을 가능하게 한다. 이 변명들은 저조한 결과가 자존감을 낮추는 것을 막는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② self-esteem: 자존감. 변명으로 저조한 결과가 '자존감'을 낮추는 것을 방지.
❌ ① reputation(평판): 가능해 보이나 원문은 self-esteem.
❌ ③ popularity(인기): 문맥 부적합.
❌ ④ intelligence(지능): 문맥 부적합.
det.tip: self-esteem: 자존감, 자아존중감 / prevent A from ~ing: A가 ~하는 것을 막다

questions.passage: As first-year students in high school, you'll sometimes face difficult moments. It is not unusual because everyone goes through difficult times. Even though you feel disappointed with your choices or behaviors, don't let yourself feel down. The most important thing is figuring out your own way to __________ your negative feelings.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 고등학교 1학년으로서 때때로 어려운 순간을 맞이할 것이다. 선택이나 행동에 실망하더라도 기죽지 마라. 가장 중요한 것은 부정적 감정을 극복할 자신만의 방법을 찾는 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② overcome: 부정적 감정을 '극복하다'. 원문 그대로.
❌ ① ignore(무시하다): 감정을 무시하라는 것이 아님.
❌ ③ intensify(강화하다): 부정적 감정을 강화하면 안 됨.
❌ ④ accept(수용하다): 가능해 보이나, 원문은 overcome(극복).
det.tip: overcome: 극복하다, 이겨내다 / figure out: 알아내다, 파악하다 / feel down: 기죽다, 우울하다

questions.passage: Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be <u>excluded</u> from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 <u>excluded</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 사람들은 또래에게서 배제되는 것을 원하지 않는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① removed: 제거된, 배제된 — excluded와 유사한 의미.
❌ ② invited(초대된): 반대 의미.
❌ ③ absorbed(흡수된, 몰두한): 의미 다름.
❌ ④ promoted(승진된, 홍보된): 의미 다름.
det.tip: exclude: 배제하다, 제외하다 ≈ remove, shut out / be excluded from: ~에서 배제되다

questions.passage: Since she wanted to get a good grade, she made a <u>thorough</u> study plan for herself. Yet, every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead. For instance, she cleaned her desk or texted her friends. These activities distracted her from studying.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 <u>thorough</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 좋은 성적을 받고 싶었기에 철저한 학습 계획을 세웠다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② detailed: 상세한, 꼼꼼한 — thorough와 유사.
❌ ① quick(빠른): thorough는 빠른 것이 아니라 꼼꼼한 것.
❌ ③ flexible(유연한): 의미 다름.
❌ ④ temporary(일시적인): 의미 다름.
det.tip: thorough: 철저한, 꼼꼼한 ≈ detailed, comprehensive / a thorough plan: 철저한 계획

questions.passage: If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the <u>challenging</u> tasks.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 <u>challenging</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 도전적인 과제를 시도하려는 마음이 더 들 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② difficult: 어려운, 힘든 — challenging과 유사.
❌ ① boring(지루한): 의미 다름.
❌ ③ familiar(익숙한): 의미 다름.
❌ ④ enjoyable(즐거운): 의미 다름.
det.tip: challenging: 도전적인, 어려운 ≈ difficult, demanding / challenging tasks: 도전적 과제

questions.passage: Following the crowd, of course, does not always lead to <u>negative</u> consequences, but it can lead to regret. So, how can you make your own choices? The first thing is to know what you really want. Although it might be different from your friends', don't be afraid to make your own choice.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 <u>negative</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 군중을 따르는 것이 항상 부정적인 결과를 초래하는 것은 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② positive: 긍정적인 — negative의 정확한 반의어.
❌ ① harmful(해로운): negative와 유의어.
❌ ③ unlikely(가능성 없는): 반의어 아님.
❌ ④ dangerous(위험한): negative와 유사한 방향.
det.tip: negative(부정적인) ↔ positive(긍정적인) / consequence: 결과

questions.passage: When people do not have the <u>confidence</u> to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their self-esteem.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 <u>confidence</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 과제를 잘 수행할 자신감이 없을 때, 성공에 대한 장애물을 만들 가능성이 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ insecurity: 불안감, 자신감 부족 — confidence의 반의어.
❌ ① assurance(확신): confidence와 유의어.
❌ ② courage(용기): confidence와 유사한 방향.
❌ ④ pride(자부심): confidence와 유사한 방향.
det.tip: confidence(자신감) ↔ insecurity(불안감, 자신감 부족) / self-esteem: 자존감

questions.passage: One day, Yubin told me about her first science quiz. Science was the <u>subject</u> that she struggled with the most. Since she wanted to get a good grade, she made a thorough study plan for herself. Yet, every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 <u>subject</u>가 이 문맥에서 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과학은 그녀가 가장 힘들어하는 과목이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 과목: 학교에서 배우는 교과목. science quiz, study plan 등 학업 문맥.
❌ ① 주제: 토론이나 글의 주제. 학업 문맥 부적합.
❌ ③ 대상: 연구 대상. 문맥 부적합.
❌ ④ 국민: 군주 아래 국민. 문맥 부적합.
det.tip: subject 다의어: ① 주제(topic) ② 과목(school course) ③ 대상(target) ④ 국민(citizen) — 문맥으로 판별

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"a mental condition in which a person creates barriers to their own success in order to protect their self-image from potential failure"

det.korean: 잠재적 실패로부터 자아상을 보호하기 위해 성공에 대한 장벽을 스스로 만드는 심리 상태.
det.analysis:
✅ ② self-handicapping: 자기 핸디캡핑. creates barriers to their own success + protect self-image.
❌ ① procrastination(미루기): 장벽을 만드는 것이 아니라 단순히 미루는 것.
❌ ③ perfectionism(완벽주의): 완벽을 추구하는 것. 장벽 만들기와 다름.
❌ ④ rationalization(합리화): 이미 일어난 일을 정당화. 사전 장벽 만들기와 다름.
det.tip: self-handicapping: 자기 핸디캡핑 = 실패할 경우 변명거리를 미리 만들어 놓는 행동

questions.passage: These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own. This __________ (psychology) phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect."
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이러한 심리적 요인들은 사람들로 하여금 군중을 따르게 만든다.
det.analysis: ✅ psychological: psychology(명사) → psychological(형용사). phenomenon을 수식하는 형용사 필요.
det.tip: psychology(n. 심리학) → psychological(adj. 심리적인) → psychologically(adv. 심리적으로) → psychologist(n. 심리학자)

questions.passage: She was frustrated that she __________ (continue) engaged in behaviors unhelpful for accomplishing her task. When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 그녀는 자신이 과제를 수행하는 데 도움이 되지 않는 행동에 지속적으로 참여한 것에 좌절했다.
det.analysis: ✅ continuously: continue(동사) → continuously(부사). 동사 engaged를 수식하는 부사 필요.
det.tip: continue(v.) → continuous(adj.) → continuously(adv.) → continuation(n.)

questions.passage: Following the crowd, of course, does not always lead to negative consequences, but it can lead to regret. So, how can you make your own choices? The first thing is to know what you really want. Although it might be different from your friends', don't be afraid to make your own choice. As long as you make the right choice for you, you will be __________ about your decision.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자신에게 맞는 선택을 하는 한, 결정에 대해 행복할 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ happy: 올바른 선택을 하면 '행복'할 것이라는 긍정적 결론.
❌ ① confused(혼란스러운): 올바른 선택 후 혼란은 부적합.
❌ ② ashamed(부끄러운): 올바른 선택 후 부끄러움은 부적합.
❌ ④ nervous(긴장한): 올바른 선택 후 긴장은 부적합.
det.tip: as long as: ~하는 한 / be happy about: ~에 대해 행복하다 / make the right choice: 올바른 선택을 하다

questions.passage: If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually __________ your self-handicapping.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과정에 더 집중하면 압박감이 줄어들고, 도전적 과제를 시도할 용기가 생긴다. 이것이 결국 자기 핸디캡핑을 멈출 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ stop: 과정 중심 사고가 자기 핸디캡핑을 '멈추게' 한다는 해결책 제시.
❌ ① encourage(격려하다): 자기 핸디캡핑을 격려한다는 것은 문맥 반대.
❌ ② strengthen(강화하다): 자기 핸디캡핑을 강화한다는 것은 문맥 반대.
❌ ③ justify(정당화하다): 자기 핸디캡핑을 정당화하는 것은 해결이 아님.
det.tip: eventually: 결국, 마침내 / stop: 멈추다, 중단하다 / ease the pressure: 압박을 줄이다
